描述_ZN: Scroll of "The Mountains and the Rain", Ming, by Zhang Lu, on silk, color, 147 cm long and 105 cm wide.　　The title of the painting, "Mountains and Rain Desire to Come," was added by later generations according to the content of the picture, but it is aptly used for this painting. The painting depicts a deep ravine, a spring, a stream, a misty cloud, and a swaying tree branch, a scene of impending rain and sudden changes in the storm. The whole painting is splashed with large brush strokes, dense with moisture, unrestrained with brushes, and full of ink and wash. The mountain peaks are formed with large horizontal dots, and the outer contours show irregular dog-tooth-like curves. The bold brushwork appropriately depicts the natural scenery of the stormy weather in a particular environment. The distant mountains are lightly painted with light ink, giving the impression that there are mountains beyond the mountains. At the foot of the mountain, the artist leaves a large blank space without a single brush stroke, and the dazzling clouds open up the spatial distance. The author uses the brush to paint the leaves in a messy way, making the branches and leaves swaying in the wind and rain vivid and charming. The whole picture, except for the figures, almost omits lines and is distinguished by the rendering of large blocks of ink.
